dedupe_keys.name: seed internet emulator python library for building emulated internets in docker

description: The SEED Internet Emulator is a Python library for building emulations of the internet, from a few networks up to hundreds of autonomous systems, that run as Docker containers on a single machine or a cluster. Users describe internet exchange points, autonomous systems, routers, BGP peering relationships, hosts and services such as DNS, web servers, botnets, Ethereum and Bitcoin blockchains in Python, and the library compiles the design into Docker Compose files; a web-based map shows the topology and packet flows live. It was created by Wenliang Du's SEED Labs at Syracuse University for security education and research, and presented at an ACM workshop in 2022 (DOI 10.1145/3563766.3564097). Lab exercises built on it cover BGP prefix hijacking, the Morris worm, DNS infrastructure and blockchain attacks. Coverage: synthetic internets of any size the hardware allows, with examples such as a mini internet and hybrid links to real networks. Format and access: source on GitHub under GPL v3 (about 3,500 commits and 290 stars when read), free. Caveats: emulated routers use BIRD and Linux containers, so scale and timing depend on the host machine; realism depends on the topology the user writes. Simulation uses: emulating route leaks, hijacks and outages of exchange points or transit providers, and training responders on cyber incidents in a safe internet copy. Related records: containerlab, GNS3, Mininet and ns-3 are other emulation or simulation tools, and CAIDA and PeeringDB data can supply realistic topologies.
